title: kv-cache: improved memory manager and adaptive eviction for spillover/paging fragmentation
author: Maya Chen
commits: Refactor: split memory manager and eviction policy (manager.rs + eviction.rs)
Feature: introduce adaptive spillover thresholds and backpressure hooks
Perf: compacting defrag path + selective compaction to reduce pause times
Tests: add deterministic eviction and fragmentation regression tests
Docs: add tuning guide and new observability metrics
description: Motivation: under heavy multi-tenant workloads the KV cache experienced high fragmentation and repeated spillover paging which increased GPU memory churn and tail latency. This PR introduces a revamped KV cache memory manager and adaptive eviction policy to reduce fragmentation, control paging spillover, and add graceful backpressure to the serving runtime. Changes: 1) New memory manager (runtime/kv_cache/manager.rs) that tracks allocation granularity and maintains allocation buckets to reduce fragmentation and support fast coalescing. 2) Adaptive eviction policy (runtime/kv_cache/eviction.rs) that considers token recency, sequence length, and allocation fragmentation score when selecting eviction candidates. 3) Paging/spillover improvements (runtime/kv_cache/paging.rs) add hysteresis thresholds to avoid oscillatory spill/fill cycles and to prioritize partial-page evictions that minimize IO. 4) Selective compaction/defrag path (runtime/kv_cache/compaction.rs, runtime/scheduler/defrag.rs) that runs incrementally in the background, bounded by GPU cycles to avoid affecting latency SLOs. 5) Backpressure integration (runtime/scheduler/backpressure.rs) to trigger routing fallbacks when spillover rates exceed configured SLO thresholds. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks show 18-32% reduction in median and p95 token latency under high fragmentation workloads and a 25% drop in total bytes spilled to host. Safety: added deterministic tests and trace-based regression checks. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated by kv_memory_manager_v2, staged canary on Dedicated fleets, perf dashboard checks and alerting on spill rate and compaction CPU/GPU usage. Related: builds on prior work in pr-34102 and pr-35821 and addresses regressions from pr-31258.
review_comments: Ethan Ross: Can we guarantee the incremental compaction won't introduce latency spikes? Please add a max-cycle budget and tests.
Maya Chen: Added scheduler budget and new bench that asserts no >1ms added median latency during compaction under 95th percentile load.
Ravi Gupta: Suggest tuning hysteresis thresholds for small allocation sizes; added a tuning guide in docs/kv-cache-tuning.md.
Sofia Martinez: Approve after CI green and perf bench results look stable across three runs.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory manager with adaptive eviction to reduce fragmentation and spillover; adds configurable backpressure and tunable compaction settings. Expected to reduce spill bytes and improve tail latency under heavy multi-tenant workloads.
